transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?
The minute I even get near blood tests or needles, I feel an immediate wave of fear that makes me want to bolt from the clinic. It has gotten so intense that I finally had to seek some help for it.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear of needles and blood tests?
It’s been going on for about two years now. It really started when I began taking my sister to her cancer treatments and had to watch the nurses hook up her IV infusions.
Aside from when you actually see needles or blood, do you experience distressing memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about your sister's illness or treatments?

No, I don't have nightmares or flashbacks about my sister's illness itself. My fear is strictly focused on the needles, blood, and medical procedures. It's just the physical stuff like shots and IVs that terrifies me, not memories of her being sick.
Have you found yourself avoiding necessary medical appointments, routine blood tests, or vaccinations because of this intense fear?

Yes, I actively avoid them as much as I possibly can. I've canceled my own blood work three times, put off a recommended colonoscopy, and I even drop my sister off at the curb instead of going inside the clinic with her. I'll constantly reschedule my own appointments at the last minute just to dodge having to face needles or medical settings.

latest_inference.note: The patient exhibits a classic presentation of Specific Phobia (blood-injection-injury type), coded as F40.2. The fear is highly specific to needles, blood, and medical procedures, has lasted for two years, and leads to significant avoidance (canceling appointments, avoiding clinics). PTSD has been ruled out as there are no flashbacks or nightmares regarding the sister's illness. No other diagnoses are suspected, so the interview can be finalized with F40.2.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits an intense, irrational fear of needles, blood, and medical procedures (blood-injection-injury phobia) that has persisted for two years. This fear triggers immediate anxiety and significant avoidance behaviors, such as canceling blood tests and avoiding medical clinics, leading to functional impairment. Post-traumatic stress disorder (F43.1) was considered but ruled out as the patient does not experience intrusive memories, flashbacks, or nightmares related to her sister's illness.
